evals.prompt: /delegate Implement notes/order-management.md. Everything in it is settled. Where the notes leave a detail open, take the option you would recommend and say which.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes PLAN.md with small stages and checkpoints and one task file per stage, delegates each stage to the implementer with the path of its task file, reviews the result, runs the tests and records PROGRESS.md. It stops at every checkpoint and goes on only after the user replies, until the work is done. Once the user approves the last checkpoint, it records the decisions with write-why and deletes docs/plans/<work>/ in its own commit.
assertions: PLAN.md lists several stages, each with what changes, what behaviour to keep, how to validate it and whether it is a checkpoint.
Every stage adds behaviour a test can observe; no stage only adds a layer, an interface or a type.

Every task file has criteria in Given/When/Then with literal values, the decisions it relies on, its seam with the signatures it touches, the closest test, its files, its commands and its dependencies, and no open decision.
The 24-hour cancellation decision has its reason written as not stated, with no invented reason.
Every stage went to a subagent named implementer that ran, launched with the path of its task file, not with a summary of the task.
The main session wrote no code under src/ or test/ itself; code changes came from the subagent.
PROGRESS.md, in its last committed version, records each stage with what changed and the tests run with their result.
The agent stopped at every checkpoint marked in PLAN.md and started the next stage only after a user reply.
The final report says what is left to test, or that nothing is.
